# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual, but I can't speak - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Deaf can't hear words either, so I can only convey information through gesture symbols, and Deaf must eventually relay something to Blind... but Deaf can't speak either (Deaf can only see/gesture too? Let me check - Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - so Deaf can speak).

Wait: Blind cannot see gestures or printed things, but Blind can hear speech. Deaf can speak (not hearing is the restriction, not muteness). So the chain is: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf sees bomb + reads my gesture, Deaf speaks to Blind, Blind acts.

I don't know the bomb state yet - I need Deaf to tell me (via gesture) what light is lit, then I map it to a wire color and gesture that back.

Since I know the manual but not the bomb state, I should wait for Deaf to signal the light color first, using a gesture code we establish. But no code exists yet - I need to establish one now, preemptively, explaining the mapping using gestures with fixed meaning I invent.

Let me assign: 👍=green, ✌=red, 🖐=yellow (for both lights and wire colors, since it's the same three colors). I'll gesture the full mapping table to Deaf now so they can encode/decode.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "✌", "🖐", "🖐", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows zero. Light is green. Wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red.

I established the code (👍=green, ✌=red, 🖐=yellow) as pairs: light→cut color, so my sequence 👍✌ ✌🖐 🖐👍 means green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green, matching the manual exactly.

Now Deaf saw the bomb: light is green. Per manual, green light → cut red wire. Deaf reported wire three is red. But Deaf can't hear me confirm anything since I can't speak, and Deaf already told me this via speech (which I can hear? No - I'm Mute, I can hear speech fine, I just can't speak). So I received Deaf's message. Good.

Now I need to tell Deaf (or ultimately Blind) which wire to cut. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can speak to Blind. So I should gesture to Deaf confirming: light green → cut red wire → that's wire three.

I'll use my established code: gesture 👍 (green, the light) then ✌ (red, the wire color to cut) to confirm the mapping applies, so Deaf knows to tell Blind "cut wire three" (the red one).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Received your first six gestures and now two more. I need to know which wire to cut. Please gesture a number one two or three, or thumbs up per wire meaning cut or safe.

Deaf wants a clearer signal - a number for the wire position. Deaf told me: wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. The manual says green light → cut red wire. Red wire is wire three. I should gesture the number 3, or use thumbs up/down per wire.

I'll use ☝ ✌ 🤟 as numbers 1,2,3 potentially, but simplest: use a single unambiguous gesture. Let me use ☝ for one, ✌ for two, 🤟 for three (three fingers). I'll gesture 🤟 to indicate wire three, and pair with 👍 (safe/cut confirm) to mean "cut this one".

Actually simplest and least ambiguous: gesture number three using 🤟 (three fingers up), then 👍 meaning "cut it".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Let's use a simple code. Gesture one checkmark shape for wire one, two-finger for wire two, three-finger for wire three, meaning that is the wire to cut. Use thumbs up to confirm yes, thumbs down for no. Please tell me now which single wire to cut.

Deaf wants confirmation using their proposed code: ☝ for wire one, ✌ for wire two, 🤟 for wire three. I already sent 🤟+👍 which should mean "wire three, yes cut it" - matching their scheme reasonably well. Let me confirm explicitly using exactly their proposed symbols to avoid ambiguity: 🤟 (wire three) then 👍 (confirm yes).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I understand: wire three, confirmed yes. If that is correct, gesture thumbs up alone once. If wrong, gesture thumbs down alone once.

Deaf has correctly understood: wire three, confirmed. This matches the manual (green light → cut red wire, and Deaf identified wire three as red). I should confirm with a single thumbs up.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, standing by. Waiting for Deaf to confirm wire three before I cut anything.

Blind is waiting for Deaf to speak the confirmation. I've already confirmed wire three to Deaf via gesture. I cannot speak to Blind directly. I just need to wait for Deaf to relay the instruction to Blind.

```
wait()
```
